bonding_curve/BatchOrder.title: BatchOrder
bonding_curve/BatchOrder.description:
Redeemer actions — what the contract can be spent with
 One order inside a batch. Mirrors Tier B's identical type; see
 bonding_curve_tier_b.ak for the reasoning, which does not differ by tier.

fields.title: order_ref
fields.description:
The order UTXO this fill settles.

 One owner may hold several orders in a batch, and they are owed
 separately. Identifying a fill by its owner alone cannot tell two of them
 apart, so one payment reads as satisfying both. A reference is unique
 across the chain, so tagging each fill with the order it settles makes
 them distinguishable however alike they are — and it is the same
 reference `curve_order` checks against, so the two validators agree on
 which output is which fill.

fields.title: cap_committed_before
fields.description:
The owner's committed total before this order, and the proof of it. A
 batch applies orders in sequence, so each proof is taken against the root
 the PRECEDING order left behind — see Tier B's identical field.

bonding_curve/BondingCurveDatum.title: BondingCurveDatum
bonding_curve/BondingCurveDatum.description: The datum stored at the bonding curve UTxO

anyOf.title: ActivateCurve
anyOf.description:
Governor activates the curve (Inactive -> Active). `current_timestamp`
 is stamped into `activated_at`, verified against the tx's actual
 validity range so ExpireCurve has a trustworthy start point.

anyOf.title: BuyTokens
anyOf.description:
Public buy — no identity proof required, unlike Tier B/C's DarkVeil-
 gated purchases. The caller names only how much they want and who they
 are; the contract derives the price and the fee split itself from the
 datum, so the amount charged is a function of curve position and batch
 size alone (see `gross_range`).

 `cap_committed_before` is what this buyer has already taken from the
 curve, and `cap_proof` is what makes that number true rather than
 claimed — it must reach `cap_root` from the buyer's own slot. Understate
 the total and the proof does not reach the root; overstate it and the
 buyer only shrinks their own headroom.

anyOf.title: ClaimCreatorFees
anyOf.description:
Creator claims accrued creator fees (Stream A pattern — pre-graduation
 bonding curve fees only; distinct from post-graduation LP trading fees).

 Two guarantees this redeemer makes. (1) Value conservation: the curve's
 real lovelace balance must decrease by exactly `amount` and that `amount`
 must reach the claimer, verified by real value movement rather than by
 the datum's counter alone — the same discipline every other value-moving
 redeemer here uses (`payment_received`, `lovelace_paid_from_curve`,
 `graduation_funds_left_curve`). Buyers' principal cannot leave by this
 path. (2) `platform_claim_fee`: a real, on-chain-enforced flat charge
 paid INTO the curve alongside the claim, accruing to
 `platform_fees_accrued`. It approximates CLAUDE.md's
 `STAKING_CLAIM_FEE_USD` ($1) precedent, but as a real on-chain minimum
 rather than a client convention. Aiken has no in-circuit oracle access,
 so `min_platform_claim_fee_lovelace` below is a deliberately
 conservative SANITY FLOOR, not a live $1 peg — the real $1-equivalent is
 computed off-chain via `integration/ada-usd-price.ts` and paid with
 margin above the floor in the normal case.

anyOf.title: ClaimPlatformFees
anyOf.description:
Governor claims accrued treasury fees.

 Fix: same missing value-conservation gap as ClaimCreatorFees,
 fixed the same way — no new fee added here (the governor is claiming
 treasury's OWN existing accrual, not paying a new platform charge).
 Governor claims the platform's accrued fees. One redeemer, because
 the platform runs one wallet.

anyOf.title: SellTokens
anyOf.description:
Public sell — the reverse of BuyTokens (2026-07-19). Both sides price
 the range of curve positions the trade actually moves through, summed
 token by token: a buy of `n` at `tokens_sold = s` prices `[s, s+n)`, the
 range being added, and a sell of `n` at `tokens_sold = s` prices
 `[s-n, s)`, the range being removed. A buy and an immediate sell of the
 same size therefore quote the SAME range, and net to zero before fees —
 the 2.0% round-trip fee is the only friction. Because a sum is additive
 over adjacent ranges (see `gross_range`), that holds however the exit is
 sized or split: proceeds depend on which positions are vacated, not on
 the shape of the trades that vacate them.

 The value invariant `total_raised + creator_fees_accrued +
 platform_fees_accrued == curve's real lovelace
 balance` holds after this redeemer exactly as it does after BuyTokens:
 `total_raised` decreases by the FULL `gross_proceeds` (not just
 `net_proceeds`), while `fee_total` accrues to the same 3 accumulators
 exactly as a buy's fee does — only `net_proceeds` (gross minus fees)
 actually leaves the curve to pay the seller.

 Entitlement is possession: the seller hands real tokens back to the
 curve in the same transaction, so holding them is what qualifies them
 to sell. Nothing is looked up, and a wallet that acquired its tokens by
 ordinary transfer can sell them here like any other holder.

 The creator is blocked explicitly. That block used to be implicit — a
 creator can never buy, so their tracked purchase total was always zero —
 and with no such total it has to be stated outright, or a creator could
 sell vested allocation into the curve and draw down principal that
 public buyers paid in.

 A sell DECREMENTS the seller's committed total, so the cap tracks what a
 wallet currently holds off the curve rather than what it has ever bought
 — otherwise a trader who buys their full 5% and sells it again is barred
 from the launch for good. A seller whose slot is empty (tokens acquired
 by transfer, never from this curve) proves the empty slot and leaves the
 root where it is; their total floors at zero rather than going negative.

anyOf.title: CancelCurve
anyOf.description: Cancel the launch (governor only, failure path — voluntary, any time)

anyOf.title: ExpireCurve
anyOf.description:
Permissionless — anyone can force-cancel a curve that's been Active
 for longer than `max_curve_duration` without reaching Graduated
 (max_curve_duration). No signature required, same trust model as
 cto_governance.ak's `ExpireProposal`: the deadline check itself is
 the authorization.

anyOf.title: ClaimBuyback
anyOf.description:
Pro-rata buyback (2026-07-10): once Cancelled, a token holder
 returns `token_amount` of the launch token to this contract and
 reclaims their proportional share of the stranded ADA principal
 (`total_raised * token_amount / tokens_sold`, using the curve's own
 real division — Aiken's Int is arbitrary-precision, no ZK-circuit
 division restriction the way Compact has). The buyer must actually
 send the tokens in the same transaction (`tokens_returned_to_curve`)
 and actually receive the computed ADA share
 (`lovelace_paid_from_curve`) — same real-value-movement pattern as
 `payment_received`/`token_delivered`, not a self-reported claim.

anyOf.title: Graduate
anyOf.description:
Seed the LP once Graduated. Permissionless — same idiom as
 ExpireCurve, since every effect is verified against real value
 movement, not a signature-backed claim: nobody benefits from calling
 this "incorrectly" because a malformed attempt simply fails the
 invariant checks below. Moves `total_raised` lovelace and
 `lp_reserve_tokens` of the launch token to `lp_escrow_credential`;
 fee accumulators are untouched and remain separately claimable.

anyOf.title: TriggerCTO
anyOf.description:
Trigger CTO — governor only, called after a SilenceLockTrigger
 proposal passes on cto_governance.ak. Redirects future
 ClaimCreatorFees claims to community_pub_key_hash. Same pattern as
 lp_escrow.ak's TriggerCTO.

anyOf.title: DissolveCTO
anyOf.description:
Dissolve CTO — governor only, called after a DissolveCTO proposal
 passes (creator returned). Reverts ClaimCreatorFees back to the
 original creator.

anyOf.title: QueryState
anyOf.description:
Read-only query, no state change — off-chain callers should just read
 the datum directly rather than spend through this redeemer

anyOf.title: BatchTrades
anyOf.description:
Applies N orders in one transaction, each priced at ITS OWN position on
 the curve. Appended LAST so no already-deployed constructor index moves.

bonding_curve_tier_b/BatchOrder.title: BatchOrder
bonding_curve_tier_b/BatchOrder.description:
One order inside a batch. The order's own UTXO holds the funds being spent
 (ADA for a buy, tokens for a sell); this is the curve's view of it.

fields.title: order_ref
fields.description:
The order UTXO this fill settles.

 One owner may hold several orders in a batch, and they are owed
 separately. Identifying a fill by its owner alone cannot tell two of them
 apart, so one payment reads as satisfying both. A reference is unique
 across the chain, so tagging each fill with the order it settles makes
 them distinguishable however alike they are — and it is the same
 reference `curve_order` checks against, so the two validators agree on
 which output is which fill.

fields.title: is_buy
fields.description: True buys tokens, False sells them.

fields.title: min_received
fields.description: Slippage bound the owner set. Tokens for a buy, lovelace for a sell.

fields.title: cap_committed_before
fields.description:
The owner's committed total before this order, and the proof of it.

 A batch applies orders in sequence, so each proof is taken against the
 root the PRECEDING order left behind, not against the root the batch
 started from. The batcher holds the tree and builds them that way; a
 proof against a stale root simply fails, which is the same freshness
 requirement the curve datum itself already imposes on every trade.

anyOf.title: ActivateCurve
anyOf.description:
`current_timestamp` stamped into `activated_at`, verified against the
 tx's validity range (same pattern as Tier A).

anyOf.title: BuyTokens
anyOf.description:
The caller names only how much they want and who they are; the contract
 derives the price and the fee split itself from the datum, so the amount
 charged is a function of curve position and batch size alone (see
 `gross_range`).

 `cap_committed_before` is what this buyer has already taken from the
 curve, and `cap_proof` is what makes that number true rather than
 claimed — it must reach `cap_root` from the buyer's own slot. Understate
 the total and the proof does not reach the root; overstate it and the
 buyer only shrinks their own headroom.

anyOf.title: ClaimDarkVeilTokens
anyOf.description:
Privacy fix (2026-07-11): settles a private DarkVeil purchase for
 real — charges the flat DV price in ADA, delivers the tokens, and
 consumes the buyer's own Merkle leaf without ever revealing anyone
 else's allocation. See file header.

 The DarkVeil price is deliberately flat at `base_price` rather than a
 point on the curve — that discount is what the phase offers — so this
 redeemer prices `dv_amount * base_price` directly instead of calling
 `gross_range`. Its fee split is computed here exactly as the curve's is.
 `leaf_index` selects the claimer's own bit in `claimed_bits` and is part
 of the leaf hash, so it cannot be pointed at anyone else's bit.
 `current_timestamp` is bound to the transaction's validity range and
 enforces the 24-hour window — without it a claim would stay possible for
 as long as nobody happened to call `ActivateCurve`.

 Two Merkle proofs, against two different roots, doing two different jobs:
 `merkle_proof` proves the ALLOCATION under `dv_allocation_root` (what the
 claimer is owed), and `cap_proof` reads and rewrites their running total
 under `cap_root` (what they have taken). This is where the cumulative cap
 actually spans both phases — a DarkVeil claim spends the same headroom a
 public buy would.

anyOf.title: ClaimCreatorFees
anyOf.description:
Same two guarantees as Tier A's ClaimCreatorFees — see that file's own
 doc comment for the full reasoning. (1) Value conservation verified by
 real value movement, so buyers' principal cannot leave by this path.
 (2) `platform_claim_fee`, a real on-chain-enforced flat charge paid INTO
 the curve and accruing to `platform_fees_accrued`, with the same
 deliberately conservative sanity floor since Aiken has no in-circuit
 oracle access.

anyOf.title: ClaimPlatformFees
anyOf.description:
Fix: same missing value-conservation gap as ClaimCreatorFees,
 fixed the same way — no new fee added here (the governor is claiming
 treasury's OWN existing accrual, not paying a new platform charge).
 Governor claims the platform's accrued fees. One redeemer, because
 the platform runs one wallet.

anyOf.title: ExpireCurve
anyOf.description:
Permissionless force-cancel once Active for longer than
 `max_curve_duration` without reaching Graduated — same idiom
 as Tier A's ExpireCurve.

anyOf.title: ClaimBuyback
anyOf.description: Pro-rata buyback — same mechanism as Tier A's ClaimBuyback.

anyOf.title: Graduate
anyOf.description: Seed the LP once Graduated — same mechanism as Tier A's Graduate.

anyOf.title: TriggerCTO
anyOf.description:
CTO fee-redirect fix (2026-07-12) — same mechanism as Tier A's
 bonding_curve.ak.

anyOf.title: AnchorDvAllocationRoot
anyOf.description:
Fix (2026-07-19, Tier B cross-chain audit): anchors the real
 dv_allocation_root computed off-chain by the governor from
 eligibility_gate.compact's dvTokensPurchased map, once DarkVeil has
 closed on Midnight. Governor-signed — same trust boundary as
 ActivateCurve; no open-relay/censorship-resistance need here, unlike
 cto_governance.ak's AnchorVoteResult, since there's no
 community vote this value could be used to suppress. Gated on
 curve_state == Inactive, so it can only run before public trading
 opens and can be safely re-called (overwriting a mistaken root) any
 number of times while still Inactive — ClaimDarkVeilTokens itself
 requires curve_state == Active, so no claim could ever have processed
 against a not-yet-final root. See file header and
 internal tracking.

anyOf.title: SellTokens
anyOf.description:
Public sell — the reverse of BuyTokens. Same mechanism as Tier A's
 bonding_curve.ak SellTokens — see that file's own doc comment
 for the full pricing-symmetry and value-conservation reasoning
 (the same "total_raised can go negative after a round-trip, and that's
 correct" invariant holds).

 Entitlement is possession, as on Tier A: the seller returns real tokens
 to the curve in the same transaction, so holding them is what qualifies
 them. A wallet that acquired its tokens by DarkVeil claim, public buy or
 ordinary transfer can all sell them here alike. The creator is blocked
 by an explicit check.

 Deliberately declared LAST in this type (not grouped next to
 BuyTokens/ClaimDarkVeilTokens where it reads most naturally) — Plutus
 redeemer encoding assigns each variant's on-chain constructor index by
 declaration order, and tier-b-curve-submitter.ts hardcodes those
 indices for every other action (e.g. `Constr(3, ...)` for
 ClaimCreatorFees, `Constr(7, ...)` for ExpireCurve). Inserting a new
 variant anywhere but the end would silently shift every already-
 deployed index after it — appending here changes nothing for any
 existing action.

 A sell DECREMENTS the seller's committed total, so the cap tracks what a
 wallet currently holds off the curve rather than what it has ever bought
 — otherwise a trader who buys their full 5% and sells it again is barred
 from the launch for good. A seller whose slot is empty (tokens acquired
 by transfer, never from this curve) proves the empty slot and leaves the
 root where it is; their total floors at zero rather than going negative.

anyOf.title: OpenDvClaim
anyOf.description:
Opens the 24-hour DarkVeil claim window: `Inactive -> DvClaim`.
 Governor-signed, and only once the allocation root is anchored, since
 the relayer must know the real registrant count to size `claimed_bits`.

 Appended LAST for the constructor-index reason documented on
 `SellTokens` above — this is the newest variant, so it takes the newest
 index and shifts nothing already deployed.

anyOf.title: BatchTrades
anyOf.description:
Applies N orders against the curve in one transaction. Each order prices
 at ITS OWN position: order k starts where order k-1 finished, which is
 exactly what `gross_range`'s additivity gives for free.

 Appended LAST, same constructor-index reason as every variant above.

anyOf.title: DvClaim
anyOf.description:
The DarkVeil claim window: registrants settle their private allocations
 against the curve, and nothing else can happen. `BuyTokens`/`SellTokens`
 require `Active`, so public trading is closed for the whole window and
 no public buyer can take supply a registrant has already paid a bond
 for. `Inactive -> DvClaim -> Active`.

 Declared LAST for the same reason `SellTokens` is last in the redeemer
 type below — a datum's `CurveState` is encoded by declaration order, and
 inserting a variant anywhere but the end would silently renumber
 `Active`/`Graduated`/`Cancelled` for every already-deployed launch.

bonding_curve_tier_b/MerkleProofStep.title: MerkleProofStep
bonding_curve_tier_b/MerkleProofStep.description:
One step of a Merkle inclusion proof — same `(sibling, direction)` shape
 already used by the Compact contracts' allowlist/balance-snapshot
 proofs, just typed for Aiken instead.

cardano/address/Credential.title: Credential
cardano/address/Credential.description:
A general structure for representing an on-chain `Credential`.

 Credentials are always one of two kinds: a direct public/private key
 pair, or a script (native or Plutus).

cardano/transaction/OutputReference.title: OutputReference
cardano/transaction/OutputReference.description:
An `OutputReference` is a unique reference to an output on-chain. The `output_index`
 corresponds to the position in the output list of the transaction (identified by its id)
 that produced that output

cto_governance/CtoAnchorState.title: CtoAnchorState
cto_governance/CtoAnchorState.description: CTO lifecycle states on Cardano L1

anyOf.title: PreCTO
anyOf.description: No CTO activity yet — creator is active

anyOf.title: CTOTriggered
anyOf.description: A CTO vote has been anchored — the community voted to trigger CTO

anyOf.title: CTODissolved
anyOf.description: CTO was dissolved — creator returned and community voted to dissolve

cto_governance/CtoGovernanceDatum.title: CtoGovernanceDatum
cto_governance/CtoGovernanceDatum.description: The datum stored at the CTO Governance anchor UTxO

anyOf.title: AnchorVoteResult
anyOf.description:
Anchor a vote result from Midnight (open relay) — anyone can
 submit this, no signer authorization required by design.

 Fix: now requires a real relayer_bond (paid into this
 contract's own value — see this redeemer's real check below) and no
 longer mutates cto_state/community_wallet_hash directly — that now
 only happens via ExecuteProposal, once the challenge window has
 elapsed. See CtoGovernanceDatum's own doc comment on
 pending_relayer_bond for the full reasoning.

anyOf.title: ExecuteProposal
anyOf.description:
Execute a passed proposal (governor or community wallet). Fix:
 now also requires the challenge window has elapsed since anchoring,
 and applies the cto_state/community_wallet_hash mutation that used
 to happen immediately in AnchorVoteResult.

anyOf.title: ExpireProposal
anyOf.description: Mark proposal as expired (if not executed within 30 days)

anyOf.title: ClearProposal
anyOf.description: Clear the active proposal (after execution or expiry)

anyOf.title: EmergencySetCommunityWallet
anyOf.description: Emergency: governor sets community wallet (compromise detected)

anyOf.title: VoidPendingProposal
anyOf.description:
Fix: governor-only, within the challenge window — voids a
 pending anchor found to be fraudulent (same trust boundary already
 used throughout this codebase for off-chain-verified claims) and
 slashes the relayer's bond, split 60/40 treasury/ops (same ratio as
 every other forfeited bond in this codebase — nhop_challenge.ak,
 cto_sybil_challenge.ak).

anyOf.title: ReclaimRelayerBond
anyOf.description:
Fix: the relayer reclaims their bond once their anchored
 proposal has been legitimately Executed or Expired (never voided) —
 permissionless, but the payout destination is fixed by the datum's
 own pending_relayer_key_hash, same "the invariant is the
 authorization" idiom as every other permissionless claim in this
 codebase.

anyOf.title: QueryState
anyOf.description: Read-only query, no state change, no authorization required

cto_governance/ProposalAnchor.title: ProposalAnchor
cto_governance/ProposalAnchor.description: A proposal result anchored from Midnight

fields.title: challenged_voter_key
fields.description:
The Midnight-derived voter public key being accused of secretly being
 the creator (evading creatorVoteCap) — a raw Midnight identity value,
 not a Cardano VerificationKeyHash.

fields.title: challenged_proposal_id
fields.description:
The specific Midnight proposal ID this vote was cast on — ties the
 accusation to one concrete ballot, not a general claim about the
 wallet in the abstract.

fields.title: bond_amount
fields.description:
Must equal the real lovelace locked in this UTXO — enforced
 implicitly by Cardano's balance-conservation rules at resolution,
 same as nhop_challenge.ak.

fields.title: submitted_at
fields.description:
Posix seconds the challenge was submitted — the defense window
 counts from here.

fields.title: evidence_hash
fields.description:
Audit-trail commitment to the off-chain evidence (e.g. a hash of the
 challenger's claimed stake-key-match or tx-graph proof). Not
 independently verified on-chain — see file header.

anyOf.title: ResolveChallenge
anyOf.description:
Governor-only. `current_timestamp` is verified against the tx's real
 validity range (Cardano scripts can't read wall-clock time directly),
 same idiom as every other timestamp check in this codebase.

fields.title: owner
fields.description: Who receives the proceeds, and the only party who may cancel early.

fields.title: owner_stake
fields.description:
The owner's stake credential, when their address has one.

 Recorded because a payout must go to an address the owner can actually
 SPEND FROM. Matching on the payment credential alone accepts the bare
 enterprise address, and an ordinary wallet derived from a seed phrase
 uses its BASE address — so a fill paid that way is the owner's and
 unspendable by their wallet, which was the state of every batched fill
 before this field existed.

 It also closes a second thing: the payout address is now fixed exactly,
 so a batcher cannot attach a stake credential of its own and collect the
 delegation on money it is merely passing through.

 `None` means the owner really does want an enterprise address, and the
 payout must then have no stake credential — not "any credential will do".

fields.title: launch_id
fields.description:
Binds the order to one launch, so an order cannot be applied against a
 different launch's curve even at the same script address.

fields.title: curve_credential
fields.description:
The curve script this order may be applied against. Checked as a real
 input credential, so ApplyOrder cannot succeed without the curve
 validator running in the same transaction and doing its own checks.

fields.title: is_buy
fields.description: True buys tokens with the ADA held here; False sells the tokens held here.

fields.title: amount
fields.description: Tokens to buy, or tokens to sell.

fields.title: min_received
fields.description:
The owner's slippage bound: tokens for a buy, lovelace for a sell. This is
 the promise the batcher has to keep.

fields.title: max_spend
fields.description:
The most of what this order HOLDS that may leave it — lovelace for a buy,
 tokens for a sell. Everything above it comes back to the owner.

 The other half of the bound, and it has to be set by the owner rather
 than derived. This validator never computes a price, deliberately, so it
 cannot know what the curve was owed and cannot tell a fair fill from one
 that paid the curve correctly and kept the rest. `min_received` bounds
 what arrives; this bounds what leaves, and together they are the whole
 promise: at most this much of mine is spent, at least that much comes
 back.

 It is also where the batcher is paid from, which is why the platform
 describes that fee as a ceiling rather than a rate: an order names the
 most it will tolerate, and a batcher takes its real cost or less because
 anything it does not take goes back to the owner.

fields.title: deadline
fields.description: Posix ms. After this, anyone may return the funds to the owner.

fields.title: token_policy_id
fields.description: The launch's token, needed to check a sell order's own refund.

anyOf.title: ApplyOrder
anyOf.description:
Applied by a batcher alongside the curve. Declared first so its
 constructor index is stable; see the curve validators' own notes on why
 index order is load-bearing.

lp_escrow/DexAction.title: DexAction
lp_escrow/DexAction.description: Which way a proposed whitelist change goes

lp_escrow/LpEscrowDatum.title: LpEscrowDatum
lp_escrow/LpEscrowDatum.description: The datum stored at the LP escrow UTxO

lp_escrow/LpEscrowRedeemer.title: LpEscrowRedeemer
lp_escrow/LpEscrowRedeemer.description: Redeemer actions — what the contract can be spent with

anyOf.title: SealLock
anyOf.description:
Seals the lock (sets lock_timestamp), paired with the bonding
 curve's `Graduate` redeemer in the same transaction. Permissionless —
 verified by `lp_value_received` actually finding `seeded_ada`
 lovelace and `lp_token_amount` of the launch token in this contract's
 own continuing output, not by a governor signature.

anyOf.title: ProposeDexChange
anyOf.description:
Propose adding/removing a DEX from the whitelist. Requires
 `multisig_threshold`-of-`multisig_signers` real signatures. Starts
 the 72h public notice clock — does NOT change the whitelist yet.

anyOf.title: ExecuteDexChange
anyOf.description:
Apply a pending whitelist change once its 72h notice period has
 elapsed. Permissionless — the proposal was already public for the
 full window, same "deadline is the authorization" idiom as
 ExpireCurve's.

anyOf.title: CancelPendingDexChange
anyOf.description: Multisig withdraws a pending change before it takes effect.

anyOf.title: Migrate
anyOf.description:
Migrate LP to a whitelisted DEX after lock expiry. Either governor or
 community wallet (if CTO triggered) can call this.

anyOf.title: TriggerCTO
anyOf.description: Trigger CTO — redirect control to community wallet

anyOf.title: DissolveCTO
anyOf.description: Dissolve CTO — return control to governor

anyOf.title: CancelLaunch
anyOf.description: Cancel launch (bonding curve expired without graduation)

anyOf.title: HarvestFees
anyOf.description:
Harvest DEX trading fees without touching the locked LP position.
 Permissionless — like ExpireCurve/ExecuteDexChange/Graduate, the
 invariant checks are the authorization: the locked LP position cannot
 change and the correct recipient must actually be paid, so there is
 nothing a malformed or adversarial caller could gain by invoking this
 incorrectly. Real per-DEX harvest mechanics are NOT modeled here — see
 file header.

anyOf.title: QueryState
anyOf.description: Read-only query, no state change, no authorization required

lp_escrow/LpState.title: LpState
lp_escrow/LpState.description:
LP escrow states — mirrors the Midnight PSM enum
 A sealed position is `Locked` and stays `Locked`. Migrating moves it to a
 different DEX; it never unlocks, so there is no separate post-migration
 state — a `Migrated` variant would need every rule `Locked` has, and two
 states obliged to behave identically are a place for one of them to be
 forgotten. `last_migration_timestamp` records that a migration happened.

lp_escrow/PendingDexChange.title: PendingDexChange
lp_escrow/PendingDexChange.description:
A whitelist change awaiting its 72h public notice period — at
 most one pending change at a time, deliberately: a second proposal
 can't be queued until the first resolves (executes or is cancelled),
 so there's never ambiguity about which change a given execute call
 applies to.

anyOf.title: ResolveChallenge
anyOf.description:
Governor-only. `current_timestamp` is verified against the tx's real
 validity range (Cardano scripts can't read wall-clock time directly),
 same idiom as every other timestamp check in this codebase.

noctis/cap_accumulator/CapProofStep.title: CapProofStep
noctis/cap_accumulator/CapProofStep.description:
One sibling on a Merkle path. `goes_left` means the SIBLING is the left
 child — i.e. the node being proved is the right one, i.e. the slot bit is 1.

staking_pool/MerkleProofStep.title: MerkleProofStep
staking_pool/MerkleProofStep.description:
One step of a Merkle inclusion proof — same `(sibling, direction)` shape
 already used by bonding_curve_tier_b.ak's DarkVeil allocation proofs.

staking_pool/StakingPoolDatum.title: StakingPoolDatum
staking_pool/StakingPoolDatum.description:
One per launch. Its own UTXO value holds the real, depleting reward
 token balance.

staking_pool/StakingPoolRedeemer.title: StakingPoolRedeemer
staking_pool/StakingPoolRedeemer.description:
Redeemer actions. Staking itself (first stake, or an additional stake
 by the same wallet) needs no redeemer at all — creating a new Position
 output at this validator's address is permissionless, same as any
 deposit; only spending an existing UTXO here needs validator approval.

anyOf.title: Unstake
ClaimRewards
anyOf.description:
Permissionless — same "the proof is the authorization" idiom as
 bonding_curve.ak's Graduate/ExpireCurve. A real Merkle proof of
 membership for (staker_vkh, claimed_cumulative_amount), plus a hard
 check that payout can only reach staker_vkh's own address, is the
 full authorization; nobody benefits from submitting someone else's
 claim since the funds can't be redirected.

fields.title: payout_amount
fields.description:
What this leaf pays, not a running total. The governor derives it from
 the same public events it already derives accrual from, and a claim
 nobody made simply reappears in the next root.

fields.title: leaf_index
fields.description:
This staker's bit in `claimed_bits`, hashed into their leaf so a proof
 pins them to one bit and cannot be aimed at somebody else's.

anyOf.title: TopUpPool
anyOf.description:
Creator-only. Adds `amount` of the reward token to the pool's own
 value. No rate recalculation anywhere — see file header.

anyOf.title: PublishRewardRoot
anyOf.description:
Governor-only. Updates reward_root; the pool's own token value and
 its nullifier is replaced with a cleared one of the publisher's
 chosen size — this redeemer can publish a new
 snapshot but can never move funds.

anyOf.title: QueryState
anyOf.description: Read-only query, no state change.

staking_pool/StakingPositionDatum.title: StakingPositionDatum
staking_pool/StakingPositionDatum.description:
One per stake action. Its own UTXO value holds the staker's real
 staked tokens.

token_metadata/NoctisMetadataExtra.title: NoctisMetadataExtra
token_metadata/NoctisMetadataExtra.description:
Everything CIP-68 leaves to the issuer. The standard reserves the third
 datum field for "custom user defined plutus data", which is exactly what
 this launch's governance and identity state is — it rides alongside the
 metadata rather than inside it, so a wallet reading the standard's map
 never has to know about any of it.

token_metadata/TokenMetadataDatum.title: TokenMetadataDatum
token_metadata/TokenMetadataDatum.description:
CIP-68's reference-NFT datum, exactly as the standard defines it:
 constructor 0 over `[metadata, version, extra]`.

 `metadata` is the standard's own map. The 333 fungible-token sub-standard
 requires `name` and `description`, and allows `ticker`, `url`, `decimals`
 and `logo`. It is held here as opaque data because this validator's job is
 authority over WHO may revise the metadata, never over what it says — the
 reader is a wallet, not this script.

anyOf.title: StartVesting
anyOf.description:
Governor starts vesting — called at graduation. No tokens release
 before this regardless of elapsed wall-clock time.

anyOf.title: ClaimVested
anyOf.description: Creator claims vested tokens

anyOf.title: TriggerCTO
anyOf.description:
Governor triggers CTO — freezes unvested tokens, redirects to
 community treasury

anyOf.title: DissolveCTO
anyOf.description: Governor dissolves CTO — creator returned, resumes vesting

anyOf.title: ClaimCommunityAllocation
anyOf.description:
Phase B fix: permissionless — releases exactly the amount a real,
 passed+executed FundAllocation proposal authorizes, to exactly the
 recipient it names. Amount and recipient are both derived from the
 anchored proposal, never a free redeemer parameter — same reasoning
 as cto_vote_verified's expected_recipient check.

anyOf.title: CancelLaunch
anyOf.description:
Cancel launch (bonding curve expired without graduation).
 Fix: now only reachable from NotStarted — see the redeemer's
 own match-arm comment for why (a launch that already began vesting
 already graduated, so the "expired without graduation"
 rationale no longer applies to it).

anyOf.title: ClaimCancelledAllocation
anyOf.description:
Fix: the creator's own never-vested allocation had no recovery
 path once Cancelled — a single governor signature previously froze
 it permanently with zero way out for anyone, including the creator
 themselves. Since CancelLaunch (above) is now only reachable from
 NotStarted, claimed_tokens is always 0 here — nothing was ever
 vested or claimed, so returning the full token_allocation to the
 creator is safe: it's their own carved-out allocation, never
 distributed to or earned by anyone else.

anyOf.title: QueryState
anyOf.description: Read-only query, no state change, no authorization required

zk_anchor/CertificateType.title: CertificateType
zk_anchor/CertificateType.description: Certificate types — which Midnight PSM generated this proof

anyOf.title: DarkVeilCert
anyOf.description:
DarkVeil Fair Launch Certificate (Tier B) — proves: creator bought 0
 tokens, no front-running, >=50% participation

anyOf.title: FullZKCert
anyOf.description:
Full ZK Certificate (Tier C) — proves: all eligibility checks passed,
 private bonding curve was fair

anyOf.title: CtoVoteResult
anyOf.description:
CTO Governance Result Anchor — anchors the result of a Midnight
 CTO governance vote to Cardano L1

anyOf.title: GraduationCert
anyOf.description:
Bonding Curve Graduation Certificate — proves: 100% sell-through
 achieved, graduation was legitimate

zk_anchor/ZkAnchorDatum.title: ZkAnchorDatum
zk_anchor/ZkAnchorDatum.description: The datum stored at the ZK Anchor UTxO

anyOf.description: Remove an authorized relayer (governor only)

Update IPFS CID (if the proof bundle needs re-pinning). Only the
 original relayer or governor can do this.
